subject: Intermittent session resets after private deployment cutover (asymmetric return path)
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: [Acme] Sessions drop ~30s after go-live to private deployment

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

We cut over our on-prem -> Redwood private link early this morning. Basic checks show connectivity is up, but our client sessions to the application terminate after ~25-35s. From the client side the TCP connection shows a clean handshake, then an RST appears coming from an unexpected source and the session tears down. No changes to the client app were made.

Quick data points:
- Occurs for both web and API traffic, TCP only, not UDP.
- Traceroute from client -> app: stable path via transitA (10.1.0.0/16).
- Packet captures on our edge show initial SYN/ACK from Redwood IPs, then RSTs from 198.51.100.12 (our firewall public SNAT pool) after ~30s.
- We suspect return path takes a different egress and triggers SNAT mapping mismatch.

Attached: pcap_snippet_20261120.pcap (just first minute) and a short traceroute capture.

Can you confirm if there are any asymmetric routing or NAT changes on Redwood side after the cutover window? This is blocking a handful of customer sessions.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reyes
Network Ops, Acme Corp

I pulled the pcap and did a quick correlation with our edge logs. Notable findings below (snippets):

--- tcpdump snippet (client -> app) ---
09:02:13.412345 IP 10.50.2.14.53872 > 172.21.10.4.443: Flags [S], seq 123456789, win 64240
09:02:13.412401 IP 172.21.10.4.443 > 10.50.2.14.53872: Flags [S.], seq 987654321, ack 123456790, win 28960
09:02:13.512789 IP 10.50.2.14.53872 > 172.21.10.4.443: Flags [.], ack 987654322, win 65535
...
09:02:43.613210 IP 198.51.100.12.12345 > 10.50.2.14.53872: Flags [R], seq 222222222
--- end snippet ---

The key thing: the RST is sourced from 198.51.100.12, which is NOT one of our Redwood balancer IPs (172.21.10.4 is the app). In our edge flow logs we see the forward path enter via transitA, but returns for a subset of flows take transitB where a different NAT pool is applied by the upstream provider. That breaks the original 5-tuple mapping and some middleboxes (firewalls) inject RST when the mapping doesn’t match.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Short-term: reduce idle timeouts and increase NAT mapping pinning on the on-prem firewall (or disable asymmetric SNAT) so return path uses same source IP.
- Better: enforce symmetric routing via BGP local-preference or prepending so the preferred return path matches the forward path.
- Longer-term: coordinate with EdgeCloud provider to move to a shared consistent SNAT pool for the private circuit.

I recommend scheduling a brief maintenance window to change the on-prem NAT behavior and apply a route-map (local-pref) to prefer transitA on the customer prefixes. I can help validate with flow logs during the window.

Jonas Weber
Senior Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme.com>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Acme] Sessions drop ~30s after go-live to private deployment

Tom — we set up a short change window tomorrow 11/24 03:00-04:00 UTC with EdgeCloud Support and your ProcureOps team to apply two coordinated changes:

1) On-prem firewall: pin NAT mappings and bump TCP idle timeout to 6m for customer prefixes (temporary).
2) Acme BGP config: add a route-map to increase local-pref for transitA for the customer prefixes to enforce symmetric egress/ingress.

Attachments: acme_route-map-diff.txt (proposed ACL + route-map) — this is the config we plan to push. EdgeCloud Support will also add a sticky SNAT profile on their egress pool.

Jonas or Sofia, please include the minimal test plan below in the change window:
- Pre-change: capture baseline flow logs and sample tcpdumps.
- Apply NAT pin + route-map.
- Validate sessions from sample client pools at +1m, +5m, +10m.
- Rollback plan: revert route-map and NAT pin if we see increased latency or path instability.

Tom, please confirm ProcureOps <<procure@acme.com>> is aware and that EdgeCloud Support will be on the call.

—Marissa

All — change completed and validated. Summary:
- We applied the NAT pin and increased idle timeout on our firewall.
- We pushed the route-map local-pref to prefer transitA.
- EdgeCloud added sticky SNAT on their egress pool.

Validation: we ran a synthetic test suite for 30 minutes post-change and saw zero session resets. Real user traffic over the last 3 hours shows no recurrence.

Attachments: none (EdgeCloud provided logs to their portal).
